profile_headline: Chief Data Scientist | Data (Big, Huge, Small, Fast, Whatever) | Cloud | Forever Student
post_content:
I have been indicating in some of my posts that cloud is not cheap for
experimentation kind of workload mostly surrounding research and data
analytics initiatives. Below is what Mark Zuckerberg started BioHub has to say
- "In our bio board meetings, one of the things we talk about is the cost of
the compute, and our AWS bill. It's interesting, the bottleneck for progress,
in medical research at this point, a lot of the cost for it, is on compute and
the data side and not strictly on the labs or how long it takes to turn around
experiments" I have been calling out enterprises embarking AI initiatives
should look at Hybrid Cloud and not all cloud. Cloud is key to scale AI
initiatives but experimentation must start on premise and burst on to cloud as
needed In one of my precious post I have shown simple cost comparison of Cloud
vs On prem over time period. Post in first comment below 👇 While in this case
genomics data is typically massive but same is true with any industry where
they deal with massive datasets. Other aspect is data gravity and security
that one needs to look at.. hashtag#datascience hashtag#cloud hashtag#bigdata
hashtag#compute
